briefing.headline: OpenAI Orion and xAI Grok-4 escalate multi-agent capabilities amid rising compute race

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs continue rapid iteration with Orion and Grok-4 pushing multi-agent frontiers. Global funding remains robust while regulatory scrutiny intensifies over deployment risks. Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production systems.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released Orion-2 with enhanced agent orchestration; xAI deployed Grok-4 on expanded Memphis cluster; DeepSeek-V4 and Meta Llama-4 variants dropped this week. Anthropic Claude 4 Opus benchmarks show gains in long-context reasoning.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines target agentic system audits.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC ramps 2nm for AI chips; Microsoft announces $15B data center expansion in Texas; Google TPU v6 clusters reach 100k scale. Energy constraints delay several EU builds.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will multi-agent coordination protocols outpace safety alignment by 2027?
